verdicts.evidence: Applied to dist and called directly: readToml(`x = "a\`) stores `"a\` at HEAD and `"a\Stryker was here!` mutated, because the ?? only fires when a backslash is the last character of the line. Through deriveCloudflareWorkers on a project whose entry file is literally named `src/index.ts\`, HEAD emits two bindings and the mutant emits none plus a `main does not resolve` note.

verdicts.evidence: `!line` is true only for the empty string, and the three matchers below it (`\[\[`, `\[`, `[A-Za-z0-9._"'-]+`) each require at least one character, so an empty line falls through to the same continue. Measured: exhaustive enumeration of 16 105 inputs over an 11-character TOML alphabet plus 1 200 fuzzed manifests gave byte-identical readToml output and byte-identical Derivations.

verdicts.evidence: `$` is load-bearing when the line carries a lone CR, which `.` cannot cross. Measured on a wrangler.toml with CR-only line endings: HEAD matches nothing and reports `no root main`, the mutant reads `main` off the first CR-delimited segment and reports `no schedule or queue consumer declared` instead.

verdicts.evidence: The line is guarded by `value.startsWith("[")`, so `value.match(/\[/g)` always returns at least one match and the `|| []` fallback is unreachable. Measured: exhaustive enumeration of 16 105 TOML inputs over an 11-character alphabet, four crafted array fixtures (opening, empty, unbalanced, unterminated-at-EOF) and 1 200 fuzzed manifests all gave byte-identical readToml output and Derivations.

verdicts.evidence: Continuation lines are joined without the separating space. Measured through deriveCloudflareWorkers on a multi-line array under `main`: HEAD resolves the entry as `[ "a" ]` and the mutant as `["a"]`, so the two crafted projects swap which one emits two bindings and which one reports `main does not resolve to a file in the project`.

verdicts.evidence: Dropping the trim keeps each continuation line's indentation inside the value. Measured on the same multi-line `main`: HEAD resolves `[ "a" ]`, the mutant `[    "a"    ]`, and the two crafted projects swap two bindings for a `main does not resolve` note.

verdicts.evidence: Storing the raw value keeps the trailing space the continuation loop appends when it stops at end of file. Measured: an unterminated `main = [` array stores `[ "a" ` instead of `[ "a"`, which changes what resolveMain looks for — the note flips from `main does not resolve to a file in the project` to `no schedule or queue consumer declared`.
